events.what_changed: Before: the State guaranteed immigrants 'and their families' equal access, on the same terms as nationals, to social services, health, work, employment and social security. After: the same list, but only 'according to the rights and obligations corresponding to each migratory category', so equality now depends on the type of residence. In force on publication.
events.passage: ARTICULO 6° — El Estado en todas sus jurisdicciones asegurará el acceso igualitario de los inmigrantes a las mismas condiciones de protección, amparo y derechos de los que gozan los nacionales, de acuerdo con los derechos y obligaciones correspondientes a cada categoría migratoria, en particular en lo referido a servicios sociales, bienes públicos, salud, educación, justicia, trabajo, empleo y seguridad social. (Artículo sustituido por art. 1º del Decreto Nº 366/2025 B.O. 29/5/2025...)

answers.implementation_then_now: 2023: I found no practice source from around 2023 on whether formally employed, permit-holding migrants actually receive contributory SIPA/ANSES benefits. The starting rating 'Sometimes' (high informality, residence periods for non-contributory pensions) is kept. 2026: what I found from 2025 (the Hivos/EU SEE alert of August 2025, and El Salto citing the IACHR's October 2025 concern) says DNU 366/2025 restricts access to rights, social security among them. These sources describe the law and general enforcement (expulsions), not documented denials of contributory benefits. I found no evidence of a shift in how ANSES treats migrants who pay contributions, so the rating stays 'Sometimes'.

answers.sourcing_note: The dating is strong. InfoLEG has the original and updated texts of Ley 25.871 art. 6 and the updated Ley 24.241 (art. 19 has no amendment note). The 1997 original, Decreto 7/2023 and the consolidated Decreto 432/97 were read on argentina.gob.ar. The Boletín Oficial annex PDFs and the CAREF 2026 report could not be opened because PDF extraction failed. Practice evidence specific to social security is missing.

El Salto: endurecimiento políticas migratorias Argentina

answers.starting_answer_concern: The 'after some period of time' rationale rests on Ley 24.241 art. 19's 30 years of contributions. That is a contribution requirement that applies equally to nationals, not a residence period for migrants. The real migrant-specific waiting periods are in the non-contributory pensions (Decreto 432/97: 20, later 10, years for disability; 40 years for old age), which are not benefits tied to a work permit. Since DNU 366/2025, art. 6 also ties equality to migratory category, which could support the 'depending on visa type' option (50). The starting answer is kept as coded.
answers.notes: No court ruling was relied on. CSJN 'Reyes Aguilera' (2007) predates the window. Court rulings against DNU 366/2025 found in search (Cámara Nacional Electoral 'Yang, Liping'; Cámara Federal Sala III) concern the naturalisation articles, not art. 6, and some date from 2026. They were not read. Art. 6 as amended stood on 1 Jan 2026 and still stands on InfoLEG. The PUAM (Ley 27.260) residence rule for foreigners was not checked.

answers.implementation_then_now: I found no practice source, for either period, on migrant workers' actual access to the unemployment insurance under Ley 24.013 (ANSES). The starting rating 'Rarely; Sometimes' reflects that the benefit requires registered employment, and many migrants work informally. The 2025 sources (Hivos alert, El Salto citing the IACHR) cover DNU 366/2025 in law and general enforcement only. With no documented shift, the rating is kept for both dates.

answers.sourcing_note: InfoLEG's updated text of Ley 24.013 carries amendment notes: arts. 112 and 114 were changed by Decreto 90/2023, art. 113 inc. c and art. 117 by Decreto 267/2006, with no later notes. Ley 25.871 art. 6 was read in its original and amended versions. I did not open Ley 26.202 or the Convention text. Practice evidence specific to unemployment benefits is missing.

El Salto: endurecimiento políticas migratorias Argentina

answers.starting_answer_concern: Ley 24.013 arts. 113 and 117 set no residence period. Entitlement depends on 6 months of contributions in the last 3 years, and benefit length on contribution time, on the same terms as nationals. So 'after a duration of stay' does not fit what the statute says. 'Yes, immediate equal access' fits the 2023 text better. After DNU 366/2025's category qualifier in art. 6, a case could also be made for the 50 option. The citation also mislabels Ley 24.013 as the 'Work Contract Act'; the Ley de Contrato de Trabajo is Ley 20.744.
answers.notes: The Migrant Workers Convention, approved by Ley 26.202, has constitutional-level primacy over statutes under art. 75 inc. 22 as a treaty, but it does not have constitutional rank. It was not re-read. The domestic-worker extension (Decreto 90/2023) widens coverage for everyone, including the many migrant women in domestic work, but it is not a migrant-specific rule. No court ruling was relied on.
